## Highest-value finding baked into the plan

The workspec's response shape is WRONG. DM-051's count path returns
`JsonResponse(body)` directly, not `response.success(data)`, so the payload is FLAT
at `resp.data.{count,stats}` — NO `.data.data` nesting, and `.claude/rules/api.md`'s
"commonly at resp.data.data" rule does NOT apply to this path. Verified twice, from
django-mojo source. Getting this backwards yields a permanently degraded strip that
still passes any test written against the same wrong assumption.

## Amendments applied at plan time (3 blocking)

1. **BLOCKING** — seed the first count from `onAfterMount()`, NOT `onInit()`.
   `onInit` runs pre-mount, so a 250ms seed timer on a slow or lazy mount
   self-terminates and latches the strip at em-dashes until the user changes a filter.
2. **BLOCKING** — base-params exclusion must mirror BOTH `setFilter` branches.
   The draft copied only the else branch; a bundle keyed on a registered daterange
   filter would disagree with what the click clears, breaking the exact guarantee
   the exclusion exists to protect.
3. **BLOCKING** — do NOT emit `scrollbar-width: thin`. It is emitted exactly once
   today (preset segment, `ListView.js:1624`) and
   `test/unit/ListView.interactions.test.js:192` pins that count at 1 — while this
   plan both ports the declaration and extends that very scenario.
4. Signature memo added — `params-changed` fires from 8 sites, 4 of which
   (page/pagesize/sort ×2) cannot change a count.
5. AbortController claim softened — `Rest.js:417` falls back to the timeout signal
   without `AbortSignal.any`; the generation guard is the real protection.
